questions.text: What is the primary goal of instruction fine-tuning?
options: To increase the vocabulary size of the base model
To teach a pre-trained model to follow user instructions and produce helpful responses
To pre-train a model from scratch on labeled data
To compress the model for deployment on edge devices
questions.explanation: Instruction fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained language model so it can understand and follow natural language instructions, producing responses aligned with user intent.

questions.text: In the Alpaca dataset format, which field contains the model's expected output?
options: instruction
input
output
context
questions.explanation: The Alpaca format uses three fields: "instruction" (the task description), "input" (optional additional context), and "output" (the desired model response).

questions.text: Which of the following are true about the ShareGPT dataset format? Select all that apply
options: It stores conversations as a list of message turns with roles
It is limited to single-turn instruction-response pairs only
It naturally supports multi-turn dialogue data
It requires a separate tokenizer to be trained from scratch
questions.explanation: ShareGPT format represents conversations as lists of turns (e.g., human/gpt roles), making it ideal for multi-turn dialogue fine-tuning. Unlike Alpaca, it is not limited to single-turn pairs.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a chat template during instruction fine-tuning?
options: To define the model's architecture and layer count
To control the learning rate schedule during training
To compress the dataset for faster loading
To format input messages with special tokens so the model distinguishes between roles
questions.explanation: Chat templates (e.g., ChatML, Llama-style) wrap messages with special tokens that indicate role boundaries (system, user, assistant), enabling the model to correctly parse multi-turn conversations.

questions.text: What does loss masking achieve during instruction fine-tuning?
options: It prevents the model from generating special tokens
It excludes prompt/instruction tokens from the loss calculation so the model only learns to generate the response
It masks out random tokens to create a denoising objective
It hides the loss value from the training logs
questions.explanation: Loss masking sets the loss to zero for prompt/instruction tokens, ensuring the model is only trained to predict the assistant's response tokens. This prevents the model from wasting capacity learning to reproduce the user's input.
